tasks.short: Check each record for missing documents and fields, check that coded diagnoses match the notes, ask clinicians to complete items, follow up overdue ones and report audit results.

steps.what: Medical records specialist reviews records for completeness of mandatory documents and fields
Medical records specialist checks the accuracy of coded diagnoses against the notes

loop.input: The coded diagnoses and procedures and the discharge letter of one record.
loop.output: A match or mismatch per code, quoting the sentence it rests on.
loop.check: Code accepts only codes present in the record, each with a quoted sentence from the discharge letter; the specialist reads each sentence and judges whether it supports the code. Records with no supporting sentence or an unclear letter go to the specialist's full manual review.
loop.stop: One pass per record; unclear records go to the specialist unflagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Diagnoses are written as free text; rules cannot compare them with codes.

steps.what: Medical records specialist checks the final task list per clinician: each missing or inaccurate item, its record and the clinician it goes to
Medical records specialist sends clinicians the items to complete: by e-mail today, as tasks in their worklist after the change
Medical records specialist follows up records still incomplete after the deadline
Medical records specialist logs audit results in a spreadsheet for compliance with regulations

tasks.design: Rules in the patient record system ({OTHER}) check every discharged record for missing signatures, consent forms, letters and codes, and the specialist reviews the flags. A bounded step compares coded diagnoses with the discharge letter and quotes the supporting sentence; the specialist judges whether each sentence supports its code, and unclear records get a full manual review. The specialist checks the complete task list per clinician before it is released to their worklists, and an audit dashboard replaces the spreadsheet. Following up overdue items stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Records were opened one by one and gaps chased by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems run completeness rules, and models can compare codes with clinical text.
tasks.still_hard: Clinicians ignore worklist tasks when busy; follow-up stays personal.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which consultant responds to a quiet word rather than a reminder.
tasks.altitude: The specialist reviews flags instead of opening every record.

reach.learn: Whether mismatch flags cut coding errors.

evidence.claim: DHD codes day admissions to ICD-10 from clinical text in 32 hospitals.
The dossier is kept 20 years and patients may ask who viewed it.
Large-scale processing of health data needs a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from discharged records to the audit report; correcting clinical content is outside.
Input contract: completeness rules set by the medical records manager; codes from the coding team; fallback is opening records by hand.
Following up overdue items and the final check keep their full time; s2 keeps 60 because the specialist reads every quoted sentence; s3 keeps 10 for the release.
Clinicians' time is outside the specialist's savings.
research_questions: How many mismatch flags does the specialist confirm?

already_counted.description: Medical records specialist reviews completeness flags.
Medical records specialist confirms mismatch flags.

incremental.description: Medical records specialist keeps the check rules current.

approvals.approved_version: The task list with each missing or inaccurate item and its record, exactly as checked by the specialist in s2c, released once to the worklist of the clinician named for each item; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many records have free-text letters with no clear sentence, so most codes go to manual review (52.7); high: letters support most codes (60.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare paper documents, scan them, link each scan to the patient and document type, check scan quality and log the batch.

steps.what: Medical records specialist sorts and prepares paper documents for scanning
Medical records specialist scans patients' health records into electronic formats
Medical records specialist links each scan to the patient and document type

loop.input: Scanned pages without a barcode label.
loop.output: Patient number, date of birth, date and document type per page.
loop.check: Code accepts the link only if patient number and date of birth match one patient in the record system and the type is on the list; the specialist looks at the first page of each auto-linked outside letter to confirm the type matches its content. Anything else goes to the specialist.
loop.stop: One pass per page; no match means the specialist links it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Letters from outside carry no barcode, and their layout varies.

steps.what: Medical records specialist checks scans for legibility and missing pages
Medical records specialist logs the batch and sets the paper aside for destruction

tasks.design: Documents printed in the hospital carry a barcode label that links the scan automatically; for outside letters, a bounded step reads patient number, date of birth and document type and links only when they match one patient, otherwise the specialist links it; the specialist confirms the type of each auto-linked letter from its first page. The scanner flags blank or skewed pages, and the batch log fills from the scan run. Preparing and scanning stay with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every scan was linked to a patient by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Scan software reads barcodes and text, and record systems can match patients.
tasks.still_hard: Handwritten and old documents are hard to read and still linked by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a document filed under the wrong patient with the same name.
tasks.altitude: The specialist handles exceptions instead of linking every scan.

reach.learn: Whether automatic linking cuts filing backlogs.

evidence.claim: Scan software reads barcodes and printed text and can match pages to patients in the record system.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.
Fax is banned for sharing medical data.

assumptions: Boundary: from paper documents to the batch log; destroying paper is outside.
Input contract: barcode labels printed by the record system; outside letters from referrers; fallback is linking by hand.

Preparing and scanning keep their full time. s3 keeps 50 because the specialist confirms each auto-linked type; s4 keeps 75 because the scanner flags only blank and skewed pages, not poor handwriting.
No page is linked without a patient match.

already_counted.description: Medical records specialist links pages with no match.

incremental.description: Medical records specialist keeps barcode labels and document types current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most outside letters fail the match and are linked by hand (13.7); high: most documents carry a barcode or match (22.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Log record requests, check the requester's identity and right to the records, decide what may be released, compile the documents, send them securely and register the release.

steps.what: Patient or lawyer sends a request for records: by letter or e-mail today, through the portal form after the change
Medical records specialist logs requests for records from patients, lawyers and agencies
Medical records specialist checks the requester's identity and authorisation
Medical records specialist decides what information may be released according to regulations
Medical records specialist compiles the requested documents from the record
Medical records specialist checks the final package: each document against the release decision, and the requester's verified address
Medical records specialist posts or e-mails the records to the requester
Medical records specialist registers the release in the disclosure log

tasks.design: Requests come in through a form in the patient portal ({OTHER}) or by secure mail and land in a request log with deadlines. The specialist checks identity and authorisation and decides what may be released; the record system then builds a package from the chosen document types and dates. Once the specialist has checked the package, it goes out by secure mail and the release is written to the disclosure log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by post, e-mail and fax, packages were printed and releases logged in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals take requests, and record systems export selected documents for secure sending.
tasks.still_hard: Requests from third parties often lack consent or a clear legal basis.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a request from an ex-partner is not authorised.

reach.learn: Whether a disclosure log speeds up audits.

evidence.claim: Patient portals take record requests, and record systems export selected documents for secure sending.
Medical data must be shared securely; fax is banned for sharing.
Health data are special category; processing them needs an exception.

assumptions: Boundary: from the request to the disclosure record; disputes are outside.
Input contract: requests from patients and third parties through the portal or secure mail; release rules set by the privacy officer; fallback is post.

Checking identity, deciding, the final package check and sending keep their time; requesters write a portal form instead of a letter (s7), so their time does not grow. s1 keeps 40 for requests by post; s4 keeps 50 because the specialist picks document types and dates.
research_questions: Are requests answered within the legal term more often?

incremental.description: Medical records specialist helps requesters who cannot use the portal.

approvals.approved_version: The release package with exactly the documents checked by the specialist in s4c, sent once by secure mail to the requester's verified address; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most requests still come by post and are logged by hand (30.5); high: most come through the portal (36.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find diagnosis, stage and treatment in the record, enter demographics, procedures and treatment dates, and ask clinicians about gaps.

steps.what: Medical records specialist reads the record for history and extent of disease

loop.input: The pathology report, imaging reports and clinic letters of one patient.
loop.output: Proposed diagnosis date, stage and extent fields, each with the sentence it comes from.
loop.check: Code accepts only values on the registry's code lists and dates inside the care episode; the specialist reads the source sentence for each proposed value and judges whether it supports it, and fills the field by hand when it does not.
loop.stop: One pass per patient; empty or conflicting fields go to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Stage and extent are written in free text in reports.

steps.what: Medical records specialist enters demographic characteristics into the computer
Medical records specialist enters diagnostic procedures and treatment dates
Medical records specialist asks the clinician about missing or unclear details
Medical records specialist checks the complete registry form: patient, diagnosis, stage, procedures and dates against the record
Medical records specialist submits the checked form to the registry

tasks.design: Demographics, procedures and treatment dates flow from the patient record system ({OTHER}) into the registry form ({PARTNER_PORTAL}); the specialist checks the complete form and submits it. A bounded step proposes stage and extent from the reports with the source sentence, and the specialist confirms every field. Asking clinicians stays with the specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every field was read from reports and typed into the registry by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Record systems export structured data, and language models can propose fields with the source sentence.
tasks.still_hard: Accuracy differs per specialty; thresholds need local checking.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that two reports describe the same tumour differently.
tasks.altitude: The specialist confirms proposed fields instead of entering them.

evidence.claim: Record systems can export structured demographics, procedures and dates to registry forms.
Logging corrections per specialist can count as staff monitoring under the works council rules.
Large-scale processing of health data needs a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient record to clarified details; registry analysis is outside.
Input contract: structured data from the record system; fallback is typing by hand.

Asking clinicians, the final check and submitting keep their full time. s1 keeps 60 because the specialist reads every source sentence; shares follow the work: reading the record for disease extent takes far longer than entering demographics.
Clinicians' time is outside the specialist's savings.
research_questions: Which share of proposed fields is confirmed unchanged?

already_counted.description: Medical records specialist confirms proposed fields.
Medical records specialist checks transferred treatment dates.

incremental.description: Medical records specialist checks a sample of transferred fields.

approvals.approved_version: The registry form with patient, diagnosis, stage, procedures and dates exactly as checked by the specialist in s6, submitted once to the registry for that care episode; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a specialty with mostly free-text reports, so few values are proposed and dates come in late (29.4); high: structured reports (48.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The medical records specialist keeps release decisions, follow-up and judgement on unclear records; opening every record, linking scans and typing fields shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A records team that reviews exceptions and audits samples instead of handling every record.
